assessments.task_description:
During Weeks 1–5, students are required to submit five weekly journal entries via Blackboard (BB) respective Fridays. These journals should reflect on learning from Weeks 1 to 5.

The purpose of this task is to encourage critical reflection on key aspects of the lecture content. Students are expected to engage critically with the concepts, theories, and ideas covered each week. This is a situated task; therefore, submissions that do not demonstrate clear relevance to the specific weekly learning context will be penalised.
assessments.submission_guidelines: Submission instructions will be given in class in week 1 and will also be available on Blackboard.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.
assessments.late_submission: A penalty of 1 grade for each 24 hour period from time submission is due will apply for up to 7 days. After 7 days you will receive a mark of 0.
assessments.additional_info: You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.

assessments.task_description:
This curriculum design project entails the preparation of a unit of work, or mini curriculum, applying the curriculum design model, proposed by Macalister and Nation (2020). In this project you will design, develop, teach (imagine) and justify a segment of a TESOL program or syllabus for a group of students for whom you are or might be responsible. Your unit design should consist of at least 3 lessons but should not exceed 5 lessons in total. Programs may be based on classes you have taught recently or classes that could be taught in EFL contexts, ELICOS, Migrant Education, schools (Pre, Primary, Secondary), or classes you’d like to teach, etc. either in Australia or overseas.

In designing your curriculum, you should address the following:

Part A.

  1. The environment for your course, considering the nature of the learners, the teachers and the teaching situation
  2. The learner group and their specific language learning needs.
  3. The principles of language teaching and learning used to guide your design.

Part B.

  1. The goals of your unit
  2. Summary content and sequencing of a series of lessons
  3. Materials used for learning
  4. Assessment of learning, both formative and summative

Part C.

  1. Reflective justification of your design, drawing clear connections between part A and Part B. In this section you should argue the relevance of your curriculum design for the teaching situation and the needs of the learner group. The choices that you make in relation to goals, content, materials and assessment processes should be clearly justified in relation to research-informed theories of language teaching and learning. You should draw on course readings and current relevant literature to support your justification.

Note that your curriculum design project should not be based on an existing English language course book.
assessments.submission_guidelines: Assignments for this course will be submitted electronically via Blackboard and using Turnitin.

assessments.task_description:
This assessment comprises two components: (1) an interactive oral micro-teaching presentation and (2) a Q&A session. Students must pass both components to successfully complete this assessment.

For the micro-teaching presentation, students will deliver an interactive lesson based on aspect(s) of the topics covered in the course that they selected for their curriculum design (Assessment 2) with help of required resources such as ppt slides. They will enact the teaching plan developed for their mini curriculum. This task is designed to reflect authentic teaching practice, as teaching will be a central responsibility in students’ future TESOL careers. Peers enrolled in the course will take on the role of students, providing an opportunity to engage in the lesson activities and learn from one another’s presentations.

Each presentation will run for 15 minutes and will be followed by a 5 to 7-minute Q&A session with peers and the lecturer/tutor. Presentations will be conducted in tutorial groups, either face-to-face or via Zoom. As part of their participation, students are required to ask at least one constructive question during a classmate’s presentation. Active engagement as an audience member will also contribute to the overall mark.

If you use AI and/or machine translation (MT) tools in preparing your presentation resources such as ppt slides, script and notes, you must provide clear and specific details about how they were used. Failure to acknowledge the use of generative AI or MT may constitute academic misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Guidelines on appropriate referencing and acknowledgement, including an example coversheet, are available here: Overview - AI tools for assignments - Library Guides at University of Queensland Library

The Q&A component is designed to uphold academic integrity and assess your understanding of relevant TESOL concepts. You are expected to ask questions following peers’ presentations and respond to questions about your own presentation spontaneously, without the use of AI tools or other materials such as slides or scripts. The use of these prohibited materials during the Q&A session may be investigated and treated as academic misconduct. Please note that questions posed to peers must be spontaneous and not pre-prepared.

Students will have to pass both micro-teaching presentation and Q&A components to pass this assessment task.

Micro-teaching presentations will commence in Week 10. The presentation schedule will be made available to students by Week 8.
assessments.submission_guidelines: You will submit your presentation slides at least one day prior to the scheduled presentation for marking purposes. You are also responsible for bringing your slides with you on the day of your presentation.
